Installation

Source: vignettes/articles/installation.Rmd
installation.Rmd

MicroBioMeta requires R >= 4.3.

Installing MicroBioMeta

While the package is in review for Bioconductor, install it from GitHub:

if (!requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("Steph0522/MicroBioMeta")

Once accepted, it will also be installable the standard Bioconductor way:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("MicroBioMeta")

Dependencies

Every package MicroBioMeta needs for its core functions (CRAN and Bioconductor packages: vegan, hillR, betapart, ALDEx2, ANCOMBC, phyloseq, ComplexHeatmap, ggplot2, and others) installs automatically with either method above — no extra steps needed for regular use.

Additional packages for the tutorials

A couple of examples in the Tutorials use packages that aren’t required by the package itself, only by that specific example:

  • qiime2R (GitHub-only) — used in the Metabarcoding/Amplicón tutorial to import .qza artifacts exported from QIIME2:

    devtools::install_github("jbisanz/qiime2R")

    This is only needed if your own data comes from QIIME2 as .qza files. If you already have plain .txt/.csv tables, you can skip it entirely and read those directly with read.delim()/read.csv().

  • networkD3 (CRAN) — used by abundance_sankey_plot() for the interactive Sankey diagram:

    install.packages("networkD3")

Troubleshooting Bioconductor packages

If BiocManager::install() isn’t already set up, run this once first:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(version = "3.19")
